front: When was the First Five-Year Plan?
back: 1953-1957, focused on heavy industry with Soviet help.

front: When was the Great Leap Forward?
How many died in the famine after the Great Leap Forward?
back: Historians' estimates range from about 15 million to over 40 million excess deaths; many cite around 30 million.
A huge unit created in 1958 combining many villages, organising farming, industry, schools and communal kitchens.
Combining private farms into collective farms owned and worked jointly under state control.

front: What was the Hundred Flowers campaign?
back: 1956-1957: Mao invited criticism; it was followed by the Anti-Rightist Campaign (1957) against critics.

front: Give three social changes under Mao.
back: Marriage Law (1950) and women in work; literacy campaigns; barefoot doctors and rising life expectancy.

front: What did the Communist Party conclude about Mao in 1981?
back: That his achievements outweighed his mistakes, while condemning the Cultural Revolution; many historians judge the human costs more harshly.
